Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
## Simulation

**Phase 1 — start:** A(10, +3), B(40, −1), C(80, −2)

- A and B close a 30 cm gap at 4 cm/s → meet at **t = 7.5 s**, at 32.5 cm.
- (B and C only close at 1 cm/s over 40 cm → t = 40 s, later; A hits 100 at t = 30 s, later.)

**Phase 2 — after t = 7.5 s:** A(32.5, −3), B(32.5, +1), C(65, −2)

- A needs 32.5/3 = 65/6 s to reach 0.
- B and C close a 32.5 cm gap at 3 cm/s → 65/6 s.

These coincide, at t = 7.5 + 65/6 = **55/3 s**. So A falls off the left end exactly when B and C meet at 130/3 cm.

**Phase 3 — after t = 55/3 s:** B(130/3, −1), C(130/3, +2) — they now separate, so no more collisions.

- C reaches 100: (100 − 130/3)/2 = 85/3 s later → t = 55/3 + 85/3 = 140/3 ≈ 46.67 s.
- B reaches 0: (130/3)/1 = 130/3 s later → t = 55/3 + 130/3 = 185/3 ≈ 61.67 s.

The last ant off is **B**, at t = 185/3 s ≈ 61.667 s.

ANSWER: 185/3
